name: Shotgunning

lead: Shotgunning, in bodybuilding and enhancement circles, means using a large number of compounds simultaneously rather than a few chosen ones. The stated aim is a bigger or leaner physique in a shorter time.
It is a practice, not a product, so no trial tests it. Medical literature on polypharmacy and on nonmedical steroid use describes how risks grow as substances are combined.

paras: Practitioners combine several categories of compounds in one course. Specifics are not given here, as they involve prescription and research drugs.

Each added compound brings its own side effects and interactions, and it becomes harder to tell which one causes a problem. Reviews of nonmedical steroid use report cardiovascular, kidney, mood and hormonal effects, which are reported to rise when steroids are taken with other drugs.

chain: Aimed at simultaneous muscle gain, fat loss and recovery
angle.text: Users who combine many compounds do so aiming for faster physique change than a single agent would give. The approach carries documented compounding risks.

lead: Shotgunning, also called a shotgun cycle, is a term in enhancement and bodybuilding communities for using many performance or physique-altering compounds together in one course, in contrast to a focused approach built around one or two. Proponents see it as a way to pursue muscle gain, fat loss and other goals at once, which is the appearance payoff they cite.

Medical sources do not study shotgunning as such. Wikipedia's summary of anabolic steroid research notes that risks increase when athletes take steroids alongside other drugs, and describes cardiovascular, kidney, mood and hormonal effects reported in nonmedical users.[1] General medical literature on polypharmacy describes how interactions rise steeply with each added drug.[2]
The word 'shotgunning' has other unrelated meanings (rapid beer drinking, smoke-sharing and others); this article covers only the multi-compound meaning.

paras: The term describes breadth rather than any particular drug list: the 'shotgun' pattern is firing many agents at once. Practitioners distinguish it from stacking a few complementary compounds.

Surveys of nonmedical anabolic steroid users cited on Wikipedia found that most are non-competitive bodybuilders and that many believe moderate use is safe; the same summary reports kidney, cardiovascular and mood findings in users and an IARC classification of probable carcinogenicity.[1] It also states that risks rise when other drugs are taken along with steroids.[1]

In clinical practice, taking several medicines at once (polypharmacy) increases the chance of side effects and drug-drug interactions, which clinicians manage by reviewing the list and adjusting it.[2]

Because many agents are active at once, adverse effects are harder to attribute, and interactions are less predictable.[2] Documented harms of nonmedical steroid use are reported in the literature.[1]
No studies found on shotgunning as a protocol. Related research on nonmedical steroid use and on polypharmacy is summarised above.[1][2]
